name: SSI2144
full_name: FatKeys Four-Pole Voltage Controlled Filter (transistor-ladder VCF)
description: Four-pole transistor-ladder voltage-controlled lowpass filter that reprises Solid State Micro Technology's SSM2044, based on Dave Rossum's patented improved-ladder topology and widely regarded as one of the best-sounding analog synth filter ICs ever made. Uses the same internal circuit as the SSM2044 with improvements by the original designer and modern process technology: minimum 10,000:1 (typ 20,000:1) frequency sweep range, on-chip resonance control with improved unit-to-unit consistency, differential signal inputs, high control feedthrough rejection, and minimized external component count. Pin connections were revised from the SSM2044 for easier PCB layout, so it is not pin-compatible with its predecessor despite sharing the same die design.

pins.name: SIG IN+
pins.description: non-inverting differential signal input; nominal ±20mV signal level, clips at ±50mV; ground unused input via a 200 ohm resistor

pins.name: SIG IN-
pins.description: inverting differential signal input; same level/clipping as SIG IN+; typically attenuated 3dB relative to SIG IN+ to prevent cancellation of in-phase signals when driving two oscillators

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: filter signal output; max output current ±300uA min/±400uA typ/±520uA max; carries a small DC offset (10uA typ, 55uA max) unless trimmed, or AC-couple with a 10uF cap for direct connection to a current-input VCA (e.g. SSI2164)

pins.name: C4A
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 4 (pairs with C4B); also the attachment point for the optional sub-audio cutoff compensation diode network (see datasheet Figure 8)

pins.name: C4B
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 4 (pairs with C4A); see C4A for sub-audio compensation note

pins.name: C3A
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 3 (pairs with C3B)

pins.name: C3B
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 3 (pairs with C3A)

pins.name: V-
pins.description: negative supply; ±4V to ±16V range, ±18V absolute max; typ 5.2mA draw

pins.name: C2B
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 2 (pairs with C2A)

pins.name: C2A
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 2 (pairs with C2B)

pins.name: C1B
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 1 (pairs with C1A)

pins.name: C1A
pins.description: differential integrating capacitor pin, pole 1 (pairs with C1B); pole 1 is the input-side pole of the ladder

pins.name: Q CTRL
pins.description: resonance control; ground-referenced current-summing input, 0 to 1000uA range; oscillation begins around 350-450uA (400uA typ); a reverse-audio-taper pot (e.g. Bourns PDB181, 90% rotation = 50% resistance) into a 26.7k series resistor is the recommended manual control network

pins.name: FREQ CTRL
pins.description: exponential frequency control; ground-referenced voltage-summing input, -19mV/octave typ sensitivity, usable range -120mV to +150mV; avoid exceeding ~175mV (see gotchas) for sub-audio cutoff use

pins.name: V+
pins.description: positive supply; ±4V to ±16V range, ±18V absolute max; typ 5.0mA draw

SSOP-16.notes: Per Sound Semiconductor SSI2144 datasheet Rev. 3.0 (January 2018), 'PIN CONNECTIONS 16-LEAD SSOP (JEDEC MO-137-AB)' diagram, page 1, top view; cross-checked against the same page's functional block diagram pin numbering. Each pole's differential cap pin pair (e.g. C1A/C1B) is a matched pair internal to one ladder stage, not two independent nodes.

extra.Icc (positive supply current): 4.0mA min, 5.0mA typ, 6.2mA max (VFC and Q CTRL grounded)
extra.Iee (negative supply current): 4.2mA min, 5.2mA typ, 6.4mA max (VFC and Q CTRL grounded)
extra.dynamic range: 92dB typ, A-weighted, noise floor to 1% THD

typical_application: Four-pole transistor-ladder lowpass VCF core for analog synthesizers: each pole produces 3dB attenuation at cutoff (24dB/octave total rolloff), with cutoff swept exponentially by the FREQ CTRL current-summing input and resonance/self-oscillation controlled by the Q CTRL current input. Differential signal inputs allow directly summing two oscillators. Output can drive an op-amp buffer or connect directly (AC-coupled) to a current-input VCA such as the SSI2164.
gotchas: split supply only, minimum +-4V; will not run from a single rail
direct successor to the SSM2044 and uses the same internal ladder circuit/sound, but pin connections were revised for PCB layout and are NOT pin-compatible with the SSM2044

at very low (sub-audio) cutoff settings, voltage above ~175mV at FREQ CTRL (pin 15) can cause ladder current to drop below the output amp's bias current, latching the output to an unrelated fixed voltage with an audible thump; normal operation only resumes below ~135mV; a matched diode-pair bias network on the C4A/C4B pins (datasheet Figure 8) fixes this for modular systems needing sub-audio sweeps

passband gain drops as Q/resonance is increased (attenuates below cutoff as resonance rises) -- part of the classic SSM2044/SSI2144 character, but can be defeated with an external LM13700-based Q VCA replacing the internal one (datasheet Figures 9 and 10) if constant DC gain is wanted instead

Q CTRL and FREQ CTRL are both ground-referenced current/voltage summing nodes, not high-impedance inputs; drive them through the resistor networks shown in the datasheet's application circuit, not directly from a low-impedance source

for accurate 1V/octave tracking during self-oscillation, a temperature-compensating resistor (e.g. Panasonic ERA-V33J102V) and V/oct trim are required; without them, oscillation pitch will drift with temperature
